root_idea.summary: A semantic field of contraction and withdrawal in aversion, with associated shuddering, fright, and dislike.
root_idea.development: The supplied lexical family links a soul shrinking from something disliked, facial contraction in anger, and the Form VIII reaction of contraction or shuddering; related nominal and adjectival forms preserve these branches.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form VIII perfect citation form.

senses.definition: To shrink or become contracted with aversion.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic construction, describes the contraction or withdrawal of hearts when God alone is mentioned.
An alternative Quranic interpretation of the same construction describing the hearts’ reaction when God alone is mentioned.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To shrink from something in dislike or hatred.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form I usage, including the expression of a soul shrinking from a disliked object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become changed and contracted in the face from anger.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form V usage describing a facial reaction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be frightened at a thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A broader Classical use of the Form VIII verb, distinct from the Quran-attested contraction and shuddering construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To dislike or hate a thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The thing may be expressed directly, without a preposition, in the reported Classical construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A state of shrinking or contraction; also quaking or shuddering, fright, or dislike and hatred.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Substantive describing the condition or disposition associated with the lexical family.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Shrinking with aversion; disliking or hating a thing; frightened or afraid.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Adjectival or active-participial use describing a person characterized by these reactions.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Form I shrinking from something in dislike or hatred is represented.
Facial change and contraction from anger are represented.
The Quran-attested contraction and shuddering interpretations, plus broader fright and dislike constructions, are represented.
The substantive senses of contraction, shuddering, fright, and aversion are represented.
The adjectival senses of aversion, dislike, and fear are represented.

cautions: The Lane passage uses a historical Quran citation rendered as “Kur xxxix 46”; it is not treated as a modern verse location. The example location 39:45:5 is used independently because it is supplied by QAC.
The Quranic shuddering sense is an alternative interpretation explicitly attached to the same Quranic construction, not a separate additional occurrence.
